T3's action book now has three new action kinds, Hide, Camouflage and Entrench (order kinds 154–156). They spend Action Capacity and the polity's two slots per window and have six new refusal codes. A war-pulse detection rule decides who sees whom: a hide multiplies the distance at which an enemy can detect the agent by its cell's terrain concealment, and camouflage multiplies it by 1/2. Compared exactly in Int128. A concealed agent is spotted when an enemy moves within that shortened distance, and its states end when it moves, retreats or attacks. An engagement log records an exact ambush flag (an attack from concealment the target's polity did not detect). Field works build up at an exact per-year rate (complete after one day, a PLACEHOLDER) and become Earthwork (cover) and Ditch (obstacle) cells, two terrain classes appended to the battle grid. A Standoff extension exists but is OFF by default. BattleWinner.Reported passes these winners to lane MOR's DA1 rise; a test shows the winner's army morale goes to 900,000 against 700,000. findings.claim:
Concealment leaks through the outcomes of orders. Refused orders cost nothing, so any polity can probe for free for enemies it does not detect, and the intended victim of a DA7 ambush can find the ambusher and escape before it strikes.

The Hide/Camouflage preconditions EnemyInContact (20) and Observed (21), and T3's Retreat contact rule, are judged against every agent of another polity, including agents the issuer's polity does NOT detect. T3's Retreat rule is unchanged by the lane, but lane AP's concealment is what makes this matter.

Refused orders are inert: no slot and no Action Capacity are spent (the lane's own Refusals_AreRecordedWithTheirCode_AndChangeNothing). So any polity can learn for free:
(i) whether an undetected hidden or camouflaged enemy stands within attack range of one of its agents (Hide or Camouflage refused 20);
(ii) whether an enemy it cannot see is watching it (refused 21);
(iii) a Retreat is also accepted only because of the undetected enemy, and it must move away from it.

An ambusher waits within attack range of its victim for at least one window (Hide → Attack is forbidden within one window). The victim can therefore locate it to within the attack range and retreat away, or move a spotter onto those cells, before it strikes.

This contradicts the principle the lane adopted in round 1 for Attack (proposal §3.3, line 187; H-AP §11.4 V05: "an order on an unseen agent fails on detection and says nothing of its distance"). It also undercuts §3.2 and §5.2: "a concealed agent is undetected by every other polity" is true of Detects, but not of what that polity can learn.

It is not disclosed. No knowledge-leak test exists; the lane's only metamorphic test is the works-partition one. ADR-037 §4's leak gate (metamorphic on hidden state) is the project precedent for exactly this check.

The fix is design (PROPOSAL), for example:
- judge contact against detected enemies only; or
- accept the order and let it end at once (begun and spotted at the same instant, cost spent) instead of refusing.

In the probe, a campaign agent (WarId -1) of a polity that does not take part in the war moves near a hidden agent and ends its hide (cause Spotted). The war enemy still does not detect the agent, but the ambush against it is lost. Such agents also count for Observed and EnemyInContact.

- ConcealEnd.Spotted summary, Concealment.cs:67: "An enemy polity detected it";
- proposal §3.1: "no enemy polity detects it now".
